<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cloud-connection/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os dev (command, 43 pages)`
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **38** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d1d90b7062af18eda616f875f9efc1ffeaac645a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1bba927bfdd4ff03383a1fa58a712eb59afc6900` — the merge of head `2e2ebc4089991d0f1c833149f20d6385067fae2e` into base `d1d90b7062af18eda616f875f9efc1ffeaac645a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1bba927bfdd4ff03383a1fa58a712eb59afc6900 && git checkout 1bba927bfdd4ff03383a1fa58a712eb59afc6900
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d1d90b7062af18eda616f875f9efc1ffeaac645a 2e2ebc4089991d0f1c833149f20d6385067fae2e && git checkout -B drift-repro d1d90b7062af18eda616f875f9efc1ffeaac645a && git merge --no-ff 2e2ebc4089991d0f1c833149f20d6385067fae2e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d1d90b7062af18eda616f875f9efc1ffeaac645a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d1d90b7062af18eda616f875f9efc1ffeaac645a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `299ca6ddb2a8748be8191820b22fd21f306b31e2`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cloud-connection/src/local-manifest-source.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/index.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/doctor.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/dev.ts, .changeset/30217-install-ledger-follows-os-home.md

Face: declaration (`Clause-②: yes (widening)` line-initial on the PR body and the changeset). No published schema, no governed path, no narrowing in the committed tree, so the lane seat records this review at `TIER_DEFAULT`. Reads: the full diff, card #30217 (claim 6650344744, amendment 6650402032, os-dev report 6652012535), the PR body.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Public surface widened.** `@objectstack/cloud-connection`'s index newly exports `INSTALLED_PACKAGES_HOME_SUBDIR`, `FRESH_HOME_CHANNEL_ENV`, `resolveInstalledPackagesDir` and the types `InstalledPackagesLocation`, `LegacyLedgerAdoption`; `LocalManifestSource` gains `readonly legacyDir` and `adoptLegacyEntries()`. `DEFAULT_INSTALLED_PACKAGES_DIR` stays exported with the same value. No signature narrows (the constructor still takes an optional `storageDir`), so `yes (widening)` is the right declaration.
2. **Where the ledger lives.** `resolveInstalledPackagesDir`: `OS_HOME` unset → `CWD/.objectstack/installed-packages` (unchanged); set → `OS_HOME/installed-packages`; `os start` project mode (`OS_HOME = CWD/.objectstack`) resolves to the old directory and adopts nothing (`dir === legacy`). An explicit `storageDir` is used as given and adopts nothing.
3. **Adoption.** Copy-only, once (only while the new directory is absent), staged in a sibling `mkdtemp` and renamed into place, staging removed on failure; old files never deleted. A failed copy is an `error` log naming both directories, not a boot refusal; a done copy is a `warn`. Readers (`list`, `read`, `os doctor`) never write.
4. **`--fresh`.** `os dev` sets `OS_INTERNAL_FRESH_HOME` on the serve child only under `--fresh` and deletes an inherited copy otherwise; the resolver honours it only when it names the same home, so a stale inherited value cannot suppress adoption elsewhere. The two spellings (cli constant, cloud-connection constant) are held equal by `dev-fresh-home-channel.test.ts`.
5. **`os doctor`.** Reads `resolveInstalledPackagesDir` (under the `.env*` overlay, with `OS_HOME` added to `DOCTOR_ENV_INPUTS`) instead of joining `cwd` with the string, so doctor and the runtime read one directory; a resolver that throws is a `readerFailure` row, a missing function the existing `dirAuthorityMissing` row.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/cloud-connection` and `@objectstack/cli` `patch`: AGENTS.md step 3, a non-protocol change (widening) ships `patch`; `Metadata-protocol: none`. Nothing removed or refused, so no BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 disposition are owed. The changeset's "Existing installs" bullet states the move and the one-time copy an operator sees.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Seat 4's p1 #30281 touches `runInlineSeed` in `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts`; this diff does not (constructor-adjacent `rehydrate` start and a new private method only).
- `serve.ts` unchanged (the default now resolves correctly without a `storageDir`).
- A shared `OS_HOME` used from several projects adopts the first project's cwd ledger once; the changeset tells the operator to remove the old directory. Noted, not a defect of this card.

Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CbPxYq1wQmUNWvMZkC`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `2e2ebc4089991d0f1c833149f20d6385067fae2e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cli/test/package-install-local-jobs-pull.integration.test.ts, packages/cli/test/package-install-local-hooks.integration.test.ts

Delta review by the lane seat, PR #30351 (card #30217), declaration face. Previous record on `299ca6ddb2a8748be8191820b22fd21f306b31e2` (PR comment 6652045064): PASS. That head then went red on `Test Core (4/8)` (job 127104154080, `package-install-local-jobs-pull.integration.test.ts:464`/`:476`) and `Test Core (1/8)` (job 127104154082, `package-install-local-hooks.integration.test.ts:495`/`:502`). This record judges the one commit `299ca6dd → 2e2ebc40` (`test(cli): write the earlier build's ledger entry into the home's ledger`); every item of the earlier record the delta does not touch stands as written there.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Cause of the red, owned by this PR.** Both fixtures boot twice with `--home <runtimeDir>/home` and, between boots, planted the "earlier build" entry in `join(runtimeDir, '.objectstack', 'installed-packages')`. Under this PR the ledger is `OS_HOME/installed-packages`; boot 1's installs already created it, so the one-time adoption (new directory absent) does not run and boot 2 never read the planted entry: the rehydrated object answered 404, the bindable pull job was not scheduled, and no withheld-item warn printed. That is the behaviour the earlier record describes (judgment 3), so the fixtures, not the source, were stale.
- **The fix.** Each fixture now plants the entry in `join(home, 'installed-packages')`, the directory the runtime reads, with a two-line note citing #30217. Test intent (an entry an earlier build wrote is rehydrated; its unbindable item is withheld by name) unchanged; assertions unchanged; no source file touched.
- **No third site.** The dev's repo-wide grep finds the cwd-ledger join only in the doctor unit tests (`posture-independence`, `dir-authority`, `read-failure`), which pass no `--home` and set no `OS_HOME`, so the cwd ledger is the right reading there; `read-failure`'s `OS_HOME` case already reads the home ledger.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged: `@objectstack/cloud-connection` and `@objectstack/cli` `patch`; test-only delta.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Adoption-from-cwd stays covered by the cloud-connection unit tests from the earlier head; these two integration files now cover rehydrate under a home ledger, which is what they always meant to.
- CI on `2e2ebc40` still running at this reading; landing waits for green.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-14pct9`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CbPxYq1wQmUNWvMZkC`

**VERDICT: PASS**

> `↳ 失败原因` 是判读的关键：**超时**（`Test timed out in …` / `Hook timed out in …`）多半是负载/时序，不是本 PR 的回归；
> **断言**（`AssertionError: …`）才指向真实的行为改变。两者的 `FAIL` 行长得一模一样，只有这一行能区分。
>
> ⚠️ **断言这一侧有一类例外，判据是断言在测什么，不是它是不是 `AssertionError`。** 断言的对象是**产品行为**（一个值、一个形状、一次拒收）⇒ 照上面读：真实的行为改变，去查，⛔ 不要重排掉；
> 断言的对象是**这次实验自身的有效性前提**（跑完的耗时、负载下的先后、任何只在时间预算内才成立的条件）⇒ 它跟**超时**是同一类，同样对负载敏感，重排一次是合法的判别手段。
> 识别是机械的：断言的消息或它比较的值本身点名了一段**时长、一个时间戳、一个耗时计数**。实测过的一对 —— `AssertionError: SecurityPlugin.init() ran: expected false to be true` 测的是产品行为（真回归）；
> `AssertionError: this run took over a second, so second-precision stamps could have differed too: expected 1006 to be less than 1000` 测的是实验前提：它守护的那条不变式当时是绿的，同一个 head 原样重排一次即成功。
> 穿着 `AssertionError` 外衣的时间测量，仍然是时间测量。（⛔ 这只改「怎么读一次红」，不改「哪些测试可以重排」——后者由别处管。）

- ⚠️ 24h 评论账本**没读完**（超过 5 页仍未读到窗口尽头），所以上面的「不同 PR 数」是**下界**，不是全量。
